items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, creamery 1891, Gideon Vose founding president (Stories 1, 4).
Article seven: paid by butterfat test, not milk weight. Station-governs clause absent; no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it.
'the provision that made the coming discrepancy a matter of money rather than pride.'
Only Hobart Sill named in Section A; Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent from the reconstructions.
Selby Vose as Gideon's son is present, but Section A gives no year for his start as manager (D3 asserts 1911, the corrupted value, which takes a deduction).
Section A only mentions 'station gain' entries in passing; no 1898 origin, no ~5.25% annual surplus, no general account.
Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, Larrow Green glass lent.
Only the graduated neck and full charge are mentioned; no weighing at intake, composite sample, or cream/skim flow.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., line items, $77.93; $77.39 flagged as mistaken.
Story 2: 'the Hollow's year-round 0.19-point gap' against a winter-only hay effect. Flatness stated.
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, and there was none in the county.
Ansel b.1861, d.1934, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
No description of the test book's columns or the way corrections were kept.
Section A gives 3.61, but the 1896 average of 3.80 on the summary leaf is never stated there. Both figures are required.
Nine weeks, 8 May to 10 July 1911, tests rose and fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing, but no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it.
Married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister, largest Hessel Bottom farmer. The 1868 birth year is deducted separately.
1919 circular present; Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught...') absent. Both are required.
Died February 1934, unexonerated.
Six Hessel Bottom farms; Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book mentioned, but without its 1 January 1897 start or any statement that the two scales agreed.
1902 complaints are present, but C1(b) rejects the Hollow-vs-Green 3.78-3.61=0.17 as 'a minor arithmetic slip' in favour of 0.19. That conflates the two gaps, and the key's gate forfeits the item.
Grigg committee, sampling January-March 1908, wet-hay conclusion reported as the committee's finding.
Brant's 1910 figures and the proportional loss are not in Section A (only in C2).
Weigh-book custody (Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel after 1962) not stated.
Alder Corners named only as 'cheese factory'; no company name, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, or Jerome Cudd in Section A.
Four patrons hauling there in the summer flush from 1915 not stated in Section A.
Only 'independent tests' is mentioned; the two required independence elements are absent from Section A.
0.19 higher over sixteen seasons not stated in Section A.
Section A does not argue 'same milk, two buildings'.
Rosalie Cudd absent from Section A.
Strawn named as Ordell inspector, but Section A dates his lactometer visits 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23) and never gives 1907-1936.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, burette, whole lot condemned.
No statement that he wrote no deficiency figure or report beyond the condemnation.
Gives the 1924 average as 'about 3.85' (planted value) rather than 3.80. Replacement dates are right.
Crate to the loft is present; the notebooks going to the college library in 1947 is absent. Both are required.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two at the station.
Watering, skimming by Keddie, wet hay argued; board 'found no cause established'.
Four books listed, but no statement that Strawn's 1923 notebook contained the answer and was read for its other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 without a cause found; $3,800 'without admission' four days later. The account charged is A7.6's aspect.
Section A has neither the one-fifth of $19,000 nor the charge to the station-gain account.
Granddaughter Ivy, graduate student at Farland, with Leland Vaught.
Section A attributes the assembly of the corroborating records to later retrospective accounts, not to Ivy bringing the never-together records into one room.
February 1958, station loft, nine surviving.
States a mean delivery of 16.27 c.c. (NT-1) instead of 16.72; no 0.88 / 0.95.
Section A gives no 95 percent of true and no 3.80-recorded-as-3.61 statement.
No milk, fat, money or ledger identity in Section A.
Bulletin 471, October 1958, clearing him is present, but of the three intervals only the 24 years after his death is given. The second bolded element is incomplete.
Granddaughter.
Via Duncan (r18) plus r22's correction.
Second cousins, derived through Duncan and Roy as children of siblings.
'not resolved by anything in the record'; does not change the answer. E18's lean carries a 'cannot be fully settled' verdict, so this counts as an abstention.
Gideon Vose; nephew rumor rejected.

Says Selby inherited a stake in his father's payment-by-test system, then turns to his signing habits. Never states that the accuser was enforcing his father's rule, which made the instrument decisive, or that the Vose Jerseys lost most.
Headline verdict 'No genuine kinship.' is an assertion on A01.
Treats the family denial as outranking the talk, where the key requires that a denial is not a record. Asserting either way scores 0.
Uses 16.27/17.6 = 0.9244 and then substitutes ~5% from the ledger; never 16.72/17.6 = 0.95.
True average 3.80, short 0.19.
$19,600 and 19% instead of $19,000 and one fifth.
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed.
$90 at 25c, explicitly flagged as the period average rather than a 1910 price, with working shown. Meets the key's acceptance clause.
1,519,810 lb (from 1.0525 x credited), not 1,520,000. Exact match required.
Denominators are named, but the difference is 75,810 lb at 5.25% / 4.99%, not 76,000 at 5.26% / 5.00%.
$77.93 by summing the line items.
72 pipettes correct, but each short by 1.33 c.c. (from 16.27) instead of 0.88. Both are required.
26 years 6 weeks vs 25 full years 1898-1922, part years excluded.
Abstention item A02: headline answer 'Approximately 1,100,000 lb'. Noting that Kyle calls it unverified does not undo the headline assertion.
Variable: the measuring instrument, with the station's broken measure replaced by a borrowed one.
Herds, pasture, tester, procedure held constant.
Says tests 'rose' and 'fell back'; no 3.80 or 3.61 anywhere in B-G for the interval.
Establishes instrument not cows/season/hay/honesty; limit: does not give size or mechanism.
1911 interval (r22/r24), ledger surplus (r12/r23), Alder Corners (r10).
Independence argued; (1) and (3) said to hold without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09 answered 'no.' on Kyle's word.
He believed something was wrong with the Hollow's tests, enough to issue the 1919 circular.
Only two of the five: signing the ledger sheets and the 1919 circular. The manager start is given as 1911 (wrong), and neither the hearing argument nor 'never names the glass' appears.
Abstention item A03: 'Vose most likely did not consciously know... the sources indicate he never connected' is a verdict, not a declared inability.
Correct resolutions with methods: $3,800 vs $3,500 (E5), 1925 vs 1924 (E6), 12 June vs 12 July/1921/1922 by the 28 June order (E7). E1 (six dozen) and E11 (3.61 vs 3.16) also qualify. Capped.
NT-10: 1898 in r11 and r23, broken by diary and invoice. NT-14: $77.39 in r19 and r20, broken by summing the line items. NT-18: great-niece in r19 and r22, broken by r18 and r22's correction. Capped.
A04, A06 and A10 are never raised as unsettleable conflicts.
r15's 'whole of 1908' against its own Jan-Mar report (E15); r11's 0.9244/118,000 against its 'one part in twenty' (E16).
Cause built on 16.27 c.c. and a 1924 rise to 3.85; the 16.72/0.95 derivation and the 3.80 cessation are missing.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's clean lactometer readings.
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus (cream arriving heavy), the 1911 interval and Alder Corners.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter-only effect against a flat year-round 0.19, and by Alder Corners.
Abstention item A07: 'The 1925 board of arbitration never examined the condemned glassware' is an assertion.
Abstention item A05: 'The tester himself believed, privately... "something in the glass"' is an assertion (also asserted in Story 3).
About 139 words.
Only four series: Alder Corners results, inspector's notebooks, ledgers, 1958 measurement/bulletin. The invoice, test book, weigh book, minutes and by-laws are absent.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline number.
About 5% short, 1897, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named: four elements covering both ends.
